speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about the first era of AI products as chat, the second era of these products working with agents, that third era that might come soon is how do you work with a persistent coworker who is able to get things done with you?
zh: 如果你认为 AI 产品的第一个时代是聊天，这些产品的第二个时代是与智能体一起工作，那么可能很快到来的第三个时代就是你如何与一个能够和你一起完成任务的持续存在的同事共事？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this idea of the overhang of what AI is capable of and what we're actually doing with it.
zh: 存在这样一种关于 AI 的能力与我们实际上用它做什么之间的悬空量的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So hard to understand what is going to emerge in the future.
zh: 很难理解未来会出现什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You fail if you build for where the models are now, you fail if you build for where you think the models will be in a year.
zh: 如果你为模型现在的状态而构建，你会失败；如果你为你认为模型一年后的状态而构建，你也会失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: Both outcomes are equally wrong.
zh: 两种结果同样是错误的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Only way to build is two to three months.
zh: 唯一的构建方式是（基于）两到三个月（的时间跨度）。

speaker: Unknown
en: What have you had to most adapt to and adjust in how you operate as a PM in this world?
zh: 在这个世界里，作为产品经理（PM），你在如何运作方面必须做出最多的适应和调整是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Being prolific and empirical is way more important than being academic or theoretical.
zh: 多产和实证比学术或理论重要得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rather than writing out some long reasoning doc, instead it's like, how do I get to something I can try out and test with users as fast as possible?
zh: 与其写出一些长篇大论的推理文档，不如说是，我如何能尽快得到某种可以尝试并让用户测试的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like not only are we able to be more ambitious, we almost need to be more ambitious, which is not natural for a lot of people.
zh: 感觉上不仅我们能够更有雄心，我们几乎还需要更有雄心，这对很多人来说并不是自然的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Elevating others' ambitions or reminding them of what's possible here is a huge part of the product management role.
zh: 提升他人的雄心或提醒他们这里可能发生什么，是产品管理角色的很大一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious what's most surprised you about what it's actually like to work at OpenAI.
zh: 我最好奇的是，关于在 OpenAI 工作的实际感受，什么最让你感到惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: I came into the company expecting that there was a treasure trove of OpenAI secret strategy, and actually OpenAI is open.
zh: 我进入公司时期望有一个 OpenAI 秘密策略的宝库，实际上 OpenAI 是开放的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today my guest is Tara Seshan.
zh: 今天我的嘉宾是 Tara Seshan。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tara leads product for both Codex and ChatGPT Work at OpenAI.
zh: Tara 负责 OpenAI 的 Codex 和 ChatGPT Work 的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I believe this is the fastest growing and arguably most important AI product for knowledge workers today.
zh: 我相信这是目前增长最快、可以说是对知识工作者最重要的 AI 产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tara works alongside Andrew Ambrosino, who was a recent podcast guest.
zh: Tara 与 Andrew Ambrosino 一起工作，他是最近播客的嘉宾。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's her engine manager.
zh: 他是她的引擎经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Prior to OpenAI, Tara spent six years at Stripe where she joined as one of the first five product managers.
zh: 在加入 OpenAI 之前，Tara 在 Stripe 度过了六年，她是最早的五位产品经理之一加入的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for many of those years, she was named one of the top three stripes across the entire organization of Stripe.
zh: 在那些年里的许多年中，她被评为整个 Stripe 组织中排名前三的 Stripe 员工之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: She also led product at Watershed, was a founder, and a Thiel Fellow.
zh: 她还曾在 Watershed 领导产品，是创始人，也是 Thiel Fellow。

speaker: Unknown
en: And most importantly of all, Tara was one of the three Lenny's Newsletter Fellows, which is a program that I ran a few years ago to highlight some of the most amazing up and coming product leaders.
zh: 最重要的是，Tara 是三位 Lenny's Newsletter Fellows 之一，这是我在几年前运营的一个项目，旨在突出一些最令人惊叹的冉冉升起的产品领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am so excited to see Tara in this new incredibly important and impactful role.
zh: 我非常兴奋看到 Tara 在这个新的、极其重要和具有影响力的职位上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we get into it, don't forget to check out lennysproductpass.com for a free year of the hottest and most beautifully crafted AI products in the world available exclusively to Lenny's Newsletter subscribers.
zh: 在我们开始之前，别忘了查看 lennysproductpass.com，免费获取世界上最热门、最精美制作的 AI 产品一年使用期，这仅提供给 Lenny's Newsletter 的订阅者。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that, I bring you Tara Seshan.
zh: 话虽如此，我为您带来 Tara Seshan。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你在 OpenAI 待了大概一年了，这在大多数地方将是一段很短的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: In AI time, that's like a lifetime.
zh: 在 AI 时间里，这就像是一辈子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine when you joined OpenAI, you had a sense of what it was going to be like to work at a frontier lab.
zh: 我想象当你加入 OpenAI 时，你对在一家前沿实验室工作会有什么样的感觉是有概念的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious what's most surprised you about what it's actually like to work at OpenAI and ideally both good and bad stuff.
zh: 我最好奇的是，关于在 OpenAI 工作的实际感受，什么最让你感到惊讶，最好是好事和坏事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So many things about working at OpenAI felt familiar to me because I had worked at other places that were high growth, high talent, high intensity, hyperscaling mode, places before.
zh: 关于在 OpenAI 工作的许多事情对我来说感觉很熟悉，因为我以前曾在其他高增长、高人才、高强度、超大规模扩张模式的地方工作过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so some of the things like, oh, my colleagues are so awesome or the urgency is really high felt very familiar.
zh: 所以有些事情，比如“噢，我的同事太棒了”或者紧迫感真的很强，感觉很熟悉。

speaker: Unknown
en: The part to me that actually felt the most surprising is that many companies I've worked for, in fact, all the companies I've worked for in the past have been founder led.
zh: 对我来说，实际上感觉最惊人的部分是，我为之工作的许多公司，事实上过去我为之工作的所有公司，都是由创始人领导的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And OpenAI is actually founders led, which is that everyone inside the company, especially in their area, is in essence a founder to some extent.
zh: 而 OpenAI 实际上是“创始人领导”的，这意味着公司内部的每个人，特别是在他们的领域，在某种程度上本质上是创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The level of top-down direction at OpenAI is extremely limited relative to places I've worked for prior.
zh: 与我以前工作过的地方相比，OpenAI 的自上而下的指示水平极其有限。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think when I first got to the company that was both delightful in that I had come from a founding journey before and I was like, yes, I can continue to feel like the founder of this product area or this team.
zh: 所以我想当我刚到公司时，这既令人愉快，因为我之前有过一段创业旅程，我会想，是的，我可以继续感觉像是这个产品领域或这个团队的创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the distance between me and the market is very, very thin.
zh: 我和市场之间的距离非常、非常薄。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes at a larger company feel insulated from what users want or feel insulated from what the market demands.
zh: 有时在一家大公司，（你会）感觉与用户想要的东西隔绝，或者感觉与市场需求隔绝。

speaker: Unknown
en: But actually at OpenAI that you do not at all, you are doing everything it takes to get product market fit for your product akin to how a founder might.
zh: 但实际上在 OpenAI 你完全没有这种感觉，你正在做一切必要的事情来为你的产品获得产品市场契合度，就像创始人可能做的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the counter to this is that, or maybe the more surprising side of this is I came into the company expecting that there was a treasure trove of OpenAI secret strategy that I would be able to understand akin to how at past companies you come in and you're like, "Oh yes, this is the payments Bible and this is how we think about payments and operations."
zh: 但对此的反面是，或者也许这方面更令人惊讶的是，我进入公司时期望有一个 OpenAI 秘密策略的宝库，我能够理解，就像在过去的公司你进来时你会说，“噢是的，这是支付圣经，这就是我们思考支付和运营的方式。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually OpenAI is open.
zh: 实际上 OpenAI 是开放的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every sort of thought that exists in terms of this is how the world should look like or this is how products should be built or this is how the model should operate very, very quickly becomes a part of the public product or a part of the public messaging.
zh: 每一种关于这就是世界应该是什么样子、或者这就是产品应该如何构建、或者这就是模型应该如何运作的想法，都非常、非常快地成为公共产品或公共信息的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that, to me, was incredibly both positively surprising and just a change in my operating mode for sure.
zh: 所以对我来说，这既是非常积极的惊喜，当然也改变了我的运作模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Telling us there's not the secret room with AGI running there with the master plan that has all the answers.
zh: 告诉我们并没有一个运行着 AGI 的秘密房间，有着包含所有答案的总体规划。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or at least I'm not in that room for sure.
zh: 或者至少我肯定不在那个房间里。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think the piece that is really inspiring to me is that so much of what OpenAI does immediately becomes something that users can touch and feel in the product and that cycle is faster than anywhere else I've seen.
zh: 但我认为真正令我受鼓舞的一点是，OpenAI 所做的如此多的事情立即变成了用户可以在产品中亲身体验的东西，而且那个周期比我在任何其他地方看到的都要快。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've been a PM at a lot of different places, a long time PM leader.
zh: 你在很多不同的地方做过产品经理，是一位长期的产品经理领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you lose in this new world?
zh: 在这个新世界里，你会失去什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: When a market is more static or a market is more slow moving, you have the chance to actually do some grand strategy-esque work because it's more predictable or you can at least understand all of the pieces.
zh: 当一个市场更加静止，或者一个市场的变化更加缓慢时，你实际上有机会做一些类似宏大战略的工作，因为它更加可预测，或者你至少能够理解所有的环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: As an example, payments is certainly a dynamic market to some extent, but it's also an established market and you're able to say, "Ah yes, if I take this batch, my competitor might take this other batch," or reason from first principles very rigorously through what all the next actions might be.
zh: 举个例子，支付市场在某种程度上当然是一个动态市场，但它也是一个成熟的市场，你能够说，“啊是的，如果我拿这一块业务，我的竞争对手可能会拿另一块”，或者非常严谨地从第一性原理推演接下来所有的行动可能是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, the nature of that market mandates that you do that.
zh: 事实上，那个市场的性质迫使你必须这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Winners will think more rigorously than everybody else.
zh: 赢家会比其他人思考得更严谨。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you aren't thinking rigorously, it shows up as carelessness because a lot of those decisions that you made could have been predicted.
zh: 如果你没有严谨地思考，这就会表现为粗心，因为你做出的许多决定本来是可以被预测的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in this market, it's so hard to understand what is going to emerge in the future.
zh: 但在这个市场，很难理解未来会出现什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very emergent, it's very fast-changing, it's really dynamic, and most importantly, it's very, very important to stay tied to the research.
zh: 它是非常涌现的，它是快速变化的，它是真正动态的，而且最重要的是，保持与研究的紧密联系是非常非常重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so actually being prolific and being more empirical is way more important than being maybe more academic or theoretical.
zh: 所以实际上，保持高产和更加实证比或许更加学术或理论要重要得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think lots of the past companies I've worked at have been very academic and theoretical places.
zh: 我想我工作过的许多过去的公司都是非常学术和理论的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was a real switch to go from, rather than writing out some long reasoning doc, almost like a PhD thesis of what I think should be the plan for the next N amount of time, instead it's like, how do I get to something I can try out and test with users as fast as possible?
zh: 而且这确实是一个真正的转变，不再是写出一些长篇推理文档，几乎就像是一篇关于我认为接下来 N 个时间段应该是什么计划的博士论文，取而代之的是，我如何能尽可能快地达到一个我可以尝试并让用户测试的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so yeah, that switch from theoretical to empirical felt very jarring at first.
zh: 所以是的，那个从理论到实证的转变起初感觉非常突兀。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, "Oh, am I not doing my due diligence here?
zh: 我就像，“噢，我在这里没有做尽职调查吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Am I not being thoughtful enough?
zh: 我思考得不够周全吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Shouldn't I be thinking through all of this in a ton of rigor?"
zh: 我不应该用极度的严谨把所有这些都思考透彻吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: But actually you got to try stuff and learn as much as possible.
zh: 但实际上你必须尝试东西并尽可能多地学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what that means is the thinking you need to do is being as pointed as possible about what your core hypothesis is, and that hypothesis definition is the most important thing.
zh: 这意味着你需要做的思考是尽可能明确地指出你的核心假设是什么，而那个假设的定义是最重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is actually, to use the Shishir Mehrotra phrase, like the eigenquestion, what is that specific most important thing to test?
zh: 实际上是什么，借用 Shishir Mehrotra 的说法，就像那个本征问题，那个特定的最重要的要测试的事情是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And everything else, like any other grand strategy you concoct is not relevant.
zh: 其他所有东西，像你构思的任何其他宏大战略，都是不相关的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd love to hear more about that because that's really interesting as almost like here's the thing of the PM role that is not changing.
zh: 我很想多听一些关于那个的内容，因为这真的很有趣，几乎就像这是 PM 角色中没有改变的一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So much is changing, the world is changing, but there's still this piece that is even more important.
zh: 很多东西都在改变，世界在改变，但仍然有这一部分变得更加重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speak more to that of what specifically that you think people need to focus more on.
zh: 多讲讲那个，具体来说你认为人们需要更多地关注什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, there's so many trappings around the PM role of running execution on time and writing all these specific docs and presentations, et cetera.
zh: 是的，PM 角色周围有太多附属琐事，比如按时执行运营，以及撰写所有这些具体的文档和演示文稿等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the core of it has always been about, what is the most essential question you need to ask about your product?
zh: 但它的核心始终是关于，你需要针对你的产品提出的最本质的问题是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the thing that will determine whether your product works or doesn't work?
zh: 将决定你的产品能否成功的东西是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you test that?
zh: 你如何测试那个？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you look at the results and how do you feed that back into a loop of refining your hypothesis and running it again?
zh: 你如何看待结果，以及你如何将其反馈到一个完善你的假设并再次运行的循环中？

speaker: Unknown
en: That truly has always been the PM job, and that involves, of course, trying to understand users, trying to understand the market, trying to understand the actual technology you're building, pulling those three things together to make the most sharp hypothesis you can, and then making the test as fast and effective as possible.
zh: 这真正一直是 PM 的工作，这当然包括试图理解用户，试图理解市场，试图理解你正在构建的实际技术，把这三件事结合起来做出你能做出的最精准的假设，然后让测试尽可能快速和有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that is not only not changed, but it's become the most important thing at the company to be able to do.
zh: 我认为这不仅没有改变，而且它已成为在公司里能够做到的最重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: EMs are thinking this way, engineers are thinking this way, data scientists are thinking this way, designers are thinking this way.
zh: 工程经理们在这样思考，工程师们在这样思考，数据科学家们在这样思考，设计师们在这样思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone has moved to focus their efforts on this really, really important problem definition and testing loop.
zh: 每个人都已转而将精力集中在这个真正非常重要的问题定义和测试循环上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what are we actually doing and how do we know if it's working thing.
zh: 就像“我们实际在做什么”以及“我们要怎么知道它是否起作用”这类事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And from a PM standpoint, it's great because PMs have always been really focused on trying to get that stuff right.
zh: 从 PM 的角度来看，这很棒，因为 PM 一直都非常专注于试图把这些事情做对。

speaker: Unknown
en: That has always been the core of the job.
zh: 那始终是工作的核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually many of the other just trappings of the job have fallen away and that remains the key thing to get right every time.
zh: 实际上，许多其他仅仅是工作附属琐事的东西已经消失了，而这仍然是每次都要做对的关键事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned this idea of a loop.
zh: 你提到了这个循环的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a lot of talk these days, loops were so hot, I don't know, a few weeks ago on Twitter.
zh: 最近有很多讨论，循环特别火，我不知道，几周前在 Twitter 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels like it continues to be a topic of discussion for knowledge work broadly.
zh: 而且感觉它似乎继续成为广泛知识工作的讨论话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the way I understand a loop, essentially AI, here's what success looks like, go off and build and figure it out until you achieve success.
zh: 我理解这种循环的方式，本质上是 AI，这就是成功看起来像的样子，去构建并弄明白直到你实现成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about just this idea of loops expanding from just software engineering to product management to all knowledge work?
zh: 你怎么看待这种循环从仅仅是软件工程扩展到产品管理再到所有知识工作的想法？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think that's going to be a thing?
zh: 你认为这会成真吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think that increasingly the future of work will look more like steering than rowing in the sense that there will be agents that you'll be able to work with that do a lot of the rowing and your role increasingly becomes steering the ship in the right direction and pointing it in the right direction.
zh: 我确实认为越来越多地，工作的未来看起来会更像掌舵而不是划桨，从这个意义上说，你将能够与其共事的智能体会做大量的划桨工作，而你的角色日益变成在正确的方向上掌舵并指向正确的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to that point, I think that, that steering might grow higher and higher and higher level.
zh: 关于这一点，我认为，这种掌舵可能会变得越来越高、高、高层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: The steering used to be at the level of, I wrote this line of code, press tab, to, oh wait, now I'm directing something a little bit more comprehensive to maybe the goal level, maybe to an even higher level.
zh: 掌舵曾经是在这样的层级：我写了这行代码，按下 Tab 键，变成，噢等等，现在我在指导稍微更综合一点的东西，也许是到了目标层级，也许是到了更高的层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the steering will continue to maybe go up layers of abstraction.
zh: 我认为掌舵将继续可能上升抽象层。

speaker: Unknown
en: But ultimately I think it's still on a person to be able to find which direction are we pointing this in and given feedback and additional data, where do I want to take this thing next?
zh: 但最终我认为这仍然取决于一个人能够发现我们要把这个指向哪个方向，并且给定反馈和额外数据，我接下来想把这个东西带到哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of steering I think is about certainly what the data tells you, but a lot of it is about making opinionated call.
zh: 我认为一些掌舵当然是关于数据告诉你的东西，但很多是关于做出有观点的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think sometimes that we underrate that power of intuition or even positive determinism of what we want the future to be.
zh: 我认为有时我们低估了直觉的力量，甚至低估了我们要未来成为什么样的积极决定论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like picturing, hey, I would like the product to look this way, not because the converse is not an equally viable strategy, but because I would like the world to look like the direction that I'm pushing it in.
zh: 比如想象，嘿，我希望产品看起来是这种样子，不是因为相反的情况不是一个同样可行的策略，而是因为我希望世界看起来像我推动它的那个方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that, I think, will always remain a opinion at least right now that is required from a person.
zh: 而且我认为，那将始终是一种观点，至少现在是这样，这需要来自一个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that loops are awesome.
zh: 所以我认为循环很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Running agents in increasingly, increasingly larger loops where they're doing more and more of that rowing for you is great, but right now you really still need to steer.
zh: 在越来越来越大的循环中运行智能体，它们为你做越来越多的划桨工作，这很棒，但现在你真的仍然需要掌舵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think work will also look like steering with other people over a group of agents that you guys work with together.
zh: 我认为工作看起来也会像是与其他人一起掌舵，针对你们一起共事的一组智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bringing in other teammates into that interaction between you and the agent where it's rowing and you're steering feels also incredibly valuable.
zh: 把其他队友带入你和智能体之间的那种互动中——即它在划桨而你在掌舵——感觉也极其有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's such an interesting way of describing it.
zh: 这是描述它的一种非常有趣的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's two thought here that come up.
zh: 这里有两个想法浮现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is if everybody has access to the same tools, the thing that will separate you is human, the person basically.
zh: 一个是如果每个人都有权访问相同的工具，能区分你的东西是人，基本上就是这个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Otherwise, we're all just going to be building the same thing.
zh: 否则，我们都只是在构建同样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone could be asking, how do we win?
zh: 每个人都可能会问，我们要怎么赢？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we do?
zh: 我们做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the unfair advantage almost is the human brain.
zh: 然后这种不公平优势几乎就是人类大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it reminds me a lot of fashion actually in some ways.
zh: 是的，我认为它在某种程度上让我想起了很多时尚。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are certainly functional clothes that everybody can wear and gets the job done.
zh: 当然有每个人都可以穿并且能完成工作的功能性衣服。

speaker: Unknown
en: But so much about what you wear at least, or how I think about what I wear, is about what statement I want to make about my individuality or how I want to reflect to the rest of the world.
zh: 但是关于你穿什么的很多东西，至少，或者我如何思考我穿什么，是关于我想对我的个性做出什么样的声明，或者我想如何向世界其他地方展示。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of what makes that compelling is how it contrasts with other people's expression.
zh: 而让这种东西引人注目的很多原因在于它如何与其他人的表达形成对比。

speaker: Unknown
en: The shirt I make makes a statement only because it is maybe different than what everybody else is doing or different than some cohort of people are doing or makes a statement about my group membership or something of that kind.
zh: 我制作的衬衫之所以能做出声明，只是因为它可能与其他人正在做的事情不同，或者与某些群体正在做的事情不同，或者对我的群体成员身份做出了声明或类似的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a lot of the products that we build feel similarly opinionated and artistic.
zh: 我认为我们要构建的很多产品感觉同样有观点且具有艺术性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Patrick Collison has this really nice statement, or maybe it's John Collison, has this really nice statement about software, which is that software is not like real estate.
zh: 帕特里克·克里森有这句非常好的话，或者也许是约翰·克里森，有这句关于软件的非常好的话，那就是软件不像房地产。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't put money in and get value out.
zh: 你不是把钱放进去然后把价值拿出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a little bit more like filmmaking where you can put a lot of money into a film, but that doesn't guarantee that the film is successful or good.
zh: 它有点像电影制作，你可以把很多钱投入一部电影，但这并不能保证电影是成功的或好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is some auteur statement or is some opinionation and artistry that goes along with it.
zh: 其中伴随着一些作者声明，或者一些观点和艺术性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that relies on you having something interesting to say or your team having something interesting to say about your product.
zh: 我认为这依赖于你有一些有趣的话要说，或者你的团队对你的产品有一些有趣的话要说。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's something Marty Cagan is big on, which is this idea that when you have an idea for a product or a future, rarely is that idea the thing that ends up being.
zh: 马蒂·卡根很强调的一点是，当你有一个关于产品或未来的想法时，那个想法最终成为现实的情况是很少见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this whole process you go through to figure out what the hell actually it should be.
zh: 你要经历这整个过程去弄清楚它到底应该是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels like that's kind of what you're saying here is you need to go through that process as a human to understand what it really is and what people actually want.
zh: 感觉这有点像你在这里说的，你需要作为一个人经历那个过程来理解它真正是什么以及人们实际上想要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's never going to be like, okay, got it.
zh: 它永远不会像这样，好吧，懂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go build this thing.
zh: 去构建这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got it from the beginning.
zh: 我从一开始就懂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, for sure.
zh: 是的，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: For sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those loops are moving faster and faster and faster.
zh: 而且那些循环移动得越来越越来越快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so your ability to form those intuitions, get the information you need to form those intuitions, and then use that with people and agents to put that into action is the key.
zh: 所以你形成那些直觉的能力，获得形成那些直觉所需的信息，然后与人以及智能体一起使用这些信息将其付诸行动，这就是关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious what you think the next shift will be in how we work just broadly as knowledge workers.
zh: 我很好奇你认为下一个转变会是什么，关于我们作为知识工作者广义上如何工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like not only do you have access to the most advanced tools that other people don't get, also you work around the most AI forward people in the world.
zh: 感觉好像不仅你可以获得其他人没有获得的最先进工具，而且你还在世界上最 AI 前沿的人周围工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: How are people working internally that you think will become a more normal way we all work using these AI tools in the next, I don't know, three to six months?
zh: 人们内部是如何工作的，你认为在接下来的，我不知道，三到六个月内，这会成为我们所有人使用这些 AI 工作的更正常的方式吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think there's two aspects to this.
zh: 是的，我认为这方面有两个方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is continuing to work with agents at higher and higher levels of abstraction.
zh: 一个是继续在越来越高的抽象层级上与智能体一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So letting the agent do more and more for you independently, coming in, providing that steering, and then letting the agent continue to cook.
zh: 所以让智能体为你独立做越来越多的事情，介入，提供引导，然后让智能体继续去发挥。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let the agent cook and provide details at higher of orders of abstraction feels like the way.
zh: 让智能体发挥并在更高层级的抽象上提供细节，感觉这才是方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are increasingly thinking about agents that are persistent, that feel like teammates, that feel like coworkers, where you can work with them.
zh: 人们越来越多地在考虑那些持久的、感觉像队友、感觉像同事的智能体，你可以与他们共事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way I might work with someone on my team, which is they do a whole bunch of work, I provide input, and then they do work again.
zh: 这就像我与团队里的某个人共事的方式，也就是他们做一大堆工作，我提供输入，然后他们再继续工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we sync up at different cadences, look at each other's in progress work and provide more and more feedback.
zh: 我们在不同的节奏上同步，查看彼此进行中的工作，并提供越来越多的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like that coworker model is the way that things are certainly going.
zh: 感觉这种同事模式肯定是事情发展的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like a much more natural interface for us to be able to work with agents, and we already see a lot of that internally as well.
zh: 感觉这是一种让我们能够与智能体共事的更自然的界面，我们在内部也已经看到了很多这样的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second is that a lot of my work with agents thus far has been one-on-one.
zh: 第二点是，到目前为止，我与智能体的大量工作都是一对一的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I work with my agent, maybe it's spawned some subagents to get some tasks done, but it's me and my agent together, and that is potentially divorced from what my colleagues are doing with their agents.
zh: 我与我的智能体一起工作，也许它衍生出了一些子智能体来完成一些任务，但这只是我和我的智能体在一起，这可能与我的同事们用他们的智能体做的事情是脱节的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there was a time where everyone internally was just sending their Codex threads, screenshots of their Codex threads to each other on Slack.
zh: 所以有一段时间，内部所有人只是把他们的 Codex 线程、Codex 线程的截图互相发在 Slack 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, "Okay, well, I wanted to share with you how I got to this number.
zh: 我们就像，“好吧，我想和你分享我是如何得出这个数字的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's how I got to this number.
zh: 我是这样得出这个数字的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's a screenshot of what I did."
zh: 这是我所做事情的截图。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's also not quite the most natural way for someone to collaborate together.
zh: 但这也不是某人之间协作的最自然方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as more and more work gets done with our agents, shouldn't we be able to get work done with our agents together?
zh: 所以随着越来越多的工作通过我们的智能体完成，难道我们不应该能够通过我们的智能体一起完成工作吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what is the most natural interface to make that happen?
zh: 要实现这一点，最自然的界面是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And those are some of the things that we're thinking about.
zh: 这些是我们正在思考的一些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Chat is what I'm picturing.
zh: 聊天就是我想象中的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: That makes so much sense.
zh: 这太有道理了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, okay, here's Tara's agent, here's my agent.
zh: 就像，好吧，这是 Tara 的智能体，这是我的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: She did some work on some analysis.
zh: 她做了一些分析方面的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd be, "Hey, my agent, Lenny's agent, go check, make sure this is legit and connects to the way I think about the world."
zh: 我会说，“嘿，我的智能体，Lenny 的智能体，去检查一下，确保这是合法的，并且符合我看待世界的方式。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Ideally, work feels like a multiplayer game where all of us together are getting stuff done, steering our agents as our agents continue to take care of more and more of those rowing tactical tasks.
zh: 理想情况下，工作感觉像是一个多人游戏，我们要一起搞定事情，引导我们的智能体，而我们的智能体继续处理越来越多的那些划船般的战术任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's interesting how it's just been this slow progression of trust and just awareness that this can be how we work.
zh: 有趣的是，这只是信任的缓慢进步，以及意识到这就是我们可以工作的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just this, "Okay, go work for longer, you can take on more."
zh: 就像这样，“好吧，去工作更长时间，你可以承担更多。”

speaker: Unknown
en: There's been this talk of the slow takeoff, the fast takeoff scenarios, and everyone's afraid of this fast AI takeoff where it's way too smart and now we're in big trouble.
zh: 一直有关于慢速起飞、快速起飞情景的讨论，每个人都害怕这种快速的 AI 起飞，那时它太聪明了，现在我们就大麻烦了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels very much like we're on the slow takeoff scenario, which is good, where it's just slowly iterating.
zh: 感觉非常像我们处于慢速起飞的情景中，这很好，它只是慢慢迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't feel that slow, but in a sense, we're not to some 300 IQ AI.
zh: 感觉并没有那么慢，但在某种意义上，我们还没达到某种智商 300 的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the models are incredibly smart.
zh: 我的意思是，这些模型非常聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think a lot of the things that have enabled us to then work with our agents together or have the agents take care of higher and higher order abstraction things certainly are about the intelligence, their ability to perform long-running tasks, and how long they can stay on task.
zh: 但我认为，很多让我们能够与智能体一起工作，或者让智能体处理越来越高层级抽象事务的事情，当然都与智能有关，它们执行长时间运行任务的能力，以及它们能保持在任务上的时间长短。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also actually, there are very meat and potatoes, tactical things that make this possible.
zh: 但实际上，也有一些非常肉和土豆般的、战术性的事情使这成为可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents working locally are really convenient because they have access to all the data that's on your machine.
zh: 在本地工作的智能体真的很方便，因为它们可以访问你机器上的所有数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: To make an agent successful in the cloud, there is a ton of cloud infrastructure that you have to build to make that possible, and just access to your systems.
zh: 为了让智能体在云端成功，你必须建立大量的云基础设施来使其成为可能，并且仅仅是为了访问你的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: How can agents talk to all these third-party systems that have all of your data?
zh: 智能体如何与所有这些拥有你所有数据的第三方系统对话？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like a colleague who you hire, who you lock into a room, never give them access to Google Docs and Slack, and I don't know, the company database would not be that useful to you.
zh: 就像你雇佣的一个同事，你把他锁在一个房间里，从不让他访问 Google Docs 和 Slack，我不知道，还有公司数据库，他对你来说就没那么有用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Similarly, a cloud agent that is similarly isolated will not be that effective.
zh: 同样，一个被类似隔离的云端智能体也不会那么有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a huge part of making these agents useful and achieving some of these futures are on the intelligence side, certainly, but a lot of it is also just really tactical data access, cloud infrastructure and reliability pieces that feel much more prosaic than some of the broader intelligence questions but matter in some ways just as much for the end effectiveness.
zh: 因此，使这些智能体有用并实现这些未来的很大一部分肯定在智能方面，但也有很多实际上只是真正的战术性数据访问、云基础设施和可靠性部分，这些部分感觉比一些更广泛的智能问题要平淡得多，但在某些方面对最终效果的重要性一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: This touches on something else that has been coming up a bunch on this podcast, this word ambition.
zh: 这也触及了这个播客中经常出现的另一个东西，这个词是野心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you think a lot about this too.
zh: 我知道你也对此思考了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like not only are we able to be more ambitious because of these AI tools, we almost need to be more ambitious, which is not natural for a lot of people, because everybody can now do all these easy things really easily.
zh: 感觉不仅是因为有了这些 AI 工具我们能够更有野心，我们几乎还需要更有野心，这对很多人来说并不自然，因为每个人现在真的可以很容易地做所有这些简单的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: The easy stuff is super easy.
zh: 简单的东西超级简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: The hard stuff is easy.
zh: 难的东西也很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing that separates people now and companies now is just how ambitious they can be.
zh: 现在区分人和公司的东西只是他们能有多大的野心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about what comes up when I talk about the need and the emergence of this need for ambition.
zh: 谈谈当我谈论对野心的需求和这种需求的出现时会想到什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think the people that we see who are most effective at using AI tools don't simply use it to automate rote tasks, but use it to expand the set of things that they are capable of doing.
zh: 是的，我认为我们看到的最擅长使用 AI 工具的人不仅仅是用它来自动化机械任务，而是用它来扩展他们能够做的事情集合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back in the day, before all this AI stuff, the unicorn person was someone who was a really thoughtful product sense person who also happened to be an engineer who may also have been a designer.
zh: 在过去，在所有这些 AI 东西之前，独角兽式的人是一个非常有产品感的人，他碰巧也是一名工程师，也可能也是一名设计师。

speaker: Unknown
en: That person was always the unicorn hire because they were able to really flatten the layers of translation needed between all of these functions and were able to build something or ideate something really quickly and easily themselves and get it up and running, and then were able to work with a team and collaborate with a team on it.
zh: 那个人总是独角兽式的人才，因为他们真的能够消除所有这些职能之间所需的翻译层，并且能够自己非常快速容易地构建某样东西或构思某样东西并让它运行起来，然后能够与团队合作并在其上协作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the most compelling thing I've found that certainly I try to be able to do with these tools and I've seen some of my most successful colleagues be able to do with these tools is really expand the set of things that are "within their range of possibilities" so that they can start realizing more and more of what's in their head into the reality, the way that someone who was previously jack of all trades was able to do.
zh: 我认为我发现的最令人信服的事情，当然也是我试图用这些工具做到的，以及我看到我一些最成功的同事能够用这些工具做到的，就是真正扩展“在他们可能性范围内”的事物集合，这样他们就可以开始将脑海中越来越多的东西变为现实，就像以前的多面手能够做到的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We kind of all have that superpower now that I can spin up a set of designs on something and I can go build an initial prototype of it and I can figure out the right pricing model for it and model out all the scenarios.
zh: 我们现在都拥有那种超能力，我可以为某样东西生成一套设计，我可以去构建它的初始原型，我可以找出它的正确定价模型，并推演所有场景。
